def-subexponential-uniform-boundary:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix a scale $c>0$. For $0\leq\lambda<1/c$, define
$$\psi_{E,c}(\lambda):=\frac{-\log(1-c\lambda)-c\lambda}{c^2}.$$
On a discrete filtered probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0},P)$, a pair of real processes $(S_t,V_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0}$ is a **one-sided sub-exponential pair at scale $c$** when $S_0=V_0=0$, $V_t\geq0$, and both processes are $\mathcal F_t$-measurable at each time, and for every $\lambda\in[0,1/c)$ there is a real process $(L_t^\lambda)_{t\in\mathbb N_0}$ that is nonnegative, integrable, and $\mathcal F_t$-measurable at each time, satisfies $\mathbb E L_0^\lambda\leq1$ and $\mathbb E[L_t^\lambda\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\leq L_{t-1}^\lambda$ almost surely for each $t\geq1$, and obeys
$$\exp\!\left(\lambda S_t-\psi_{E,c}(\lambda)V_t\right)\leq L_t^\lambda\quad\text{almost surely for every }t\geq0.$$

For $\alpha\in(0,1)$, a Borel-measurable function $u:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is a **one-sided sub-exponential uniform boundary with crossing probability $\alpha$ and scale $c$** if, for every discrete filtered probability space and every one-sided sub-exponential pair at scale $c$,
$$P\!\left(\exists t\geq1:S_t\geq u(V_t)\right)\leq\alpha.$$
def-time-varying-target-confidence-seque:
## Definition

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0},P)$ be a discrete filtered probability space and let $(\theta_t)_{t\geq1}$ be a real target process with each $\theta_t$ measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_t$. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$, a sequence of random closed intervals $C_t=[L_t,U_t]$, with finite real $\mathcal F_t$-measurable endpoints at each $t\geq1$, is a **$(1-\alpha)$ confidence sequence for the target process $(\theta_t)$** if
$$P\!\left(\theta_t\in C_t\text{ for every }t\geq1\right)\geq1-\alpha.$$
The target may be random and may vary with time; the definition asserts only simultaneous coverage under the specified probability law.
alg-empirical-bernstein-confidence-seque:
## Definition

Inputs are real bounds $a\leq b$, a nominal error level $\delta\in(0,1)$, an observation stream $(X_t)_{t\geq1}$ with $X_t\in[a,b]$ almost surely and $X_t$ measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_t$, a forecast stream $(\widehat X_t)_{t\geq1}$ with $\widehat X_t\in[a,b]$ almost surely and $\widehat X_t$ measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_{t-1}$, and, when $c=b-a>0$, an evaluation procedure for a Borel one-sided sub-exponential uniform boundary $u_{\delta/2,c}$ with crossing probability $\delta/2$ and scale $c$. The output is one interval $C_t$ at each positive integer time $t$.

1. If $c=0$, return $C_t=[a,a]$ at each time.

2. If $c>0$, initialize $\bar X_0=0$ and $V_0=0$. After receiving forecast $\widehat X_t$ and then observation $X_t$, update
$$\bar X_t=\left(1-\frac1t\right)\bar X_{t-1}+\frac{X_t}{t},\qquad V_t=V_{t-1}+(X_t-\widehat X_t)^2.$$
Return
$$C_t=\left[\bar X_t-\frac{u_{\delta/2,c}(V_t)}{t},\;\bar X_t+\frac{u_{\delta/2,c}(V_t)}{t}\right].$$

The procedure uses observations only through time $t$. The accumulated quantity $V_t$ is the observed sum of squared forecast errors; it is not a predictable conditional-variance process.
thm-empirical-bernstein-confidence-seque:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0},P)$ be a discrete filtered probability space, let $a\leq b$ be real numbers, and put $c=b-a$. Let $(X_t)_{t\geq1}$ be real with $X_t$ measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_t$ and $P(a\leq X_t\leq b)=1$ for every $t$. Let $(\widehat X_t)_{t\geq1}$ be real with $\widehat X_t$ measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_{t-1}$ and $P(a\leq\widehat X_t\leq b)=1$ for every $t$. Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ and write $\alpha=\delta/2$. For $c>0$, let $u_{\alpha,c}$ be any Borel one-sided sub-exponential uniform boundary with crossing probability $\alpha$ at scale $c$. Choose any versions $m_t=E[X_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]$ and define
$$\bar X_t=\frac1t\sum_{i=1}^tX_i,\qquad \mu_t=\frac1t\sum_{i=1}^tm_i,\qquad V_t=\sum_{i=1}^t(X_i-\widehat X_i)^2.$$
Let $C_t$ be the interval returned at time $t$ by the empirical-Bernstein interval-update algorithm, using $u_{\alpha,c}$ when $c>0$. Then
$$P\!\left(\mu_t\in C_t\text{ for every }t\geq1\right)\geq1-\delta.$$
The probability statement is independent of the chosen conditional-expectation versions. No common conditional mean is assumed. If there is a fixed real $\mu$ such that $E[X_i\mid\mathcal F_{i-1}]=\mu$ almost surely for every $i$, then $\mu_t=\mu$ simultaneously almost surely and the same intervals cover this fixed mean.

For $c>0$, the finite-mixture formula also supplies a valid boundary: choose an integer $J\geq1$, numbers $0<\lambda_j<1/c$, and weights $w_j>0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j=1$. For every $v\geq0$, the unique nonnegative solution $s=u_{\alpha,c}(v)$ of
$$\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j\exp\!\left(\lambda_js-\psi_{E,c}(\lambda_j)v\right)=\frac1\alpha$$
defines a Borel one-sided sub-exponential uniform boundary with crossing probability $\alpha$ at scale $c$.
